question.text: What makes a freeway different from other roads?

answer.text: Freeways are multi-lane, controlled-access, divided highways with no stops and no cross traffic, built for long trips with less fatigue and more safety.

teaching.text: Freeways are divided, controlled-access highways with several lanes and no stops or cross traffic, built for safer long trips. Remember: no stops, no cross traffic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Freeways are multi-lane, controlled-access, divided highways with no stops and no cross traffic, built for long trips with less fatigue and more safety.

question.text: What does safe freeway driving require, and where must slower vehicles drive?

answer.text: Safe freeway driving means keeping pace with traffic and staying alert, and vehicles moving slower than the normal flow must keep to the right.

teaching.text: Keep up with traffic and stay alert, and if you are slower than the flow, keep to the right lanes. Remember: slower traffic keeps right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Safe freeway driving means keeping pace with traffic and staying alert, and vehicles moving slower than the normal flow must keep to the right.

question.text: Why should you avoid weaving between freeway lanes?

answer.text: Weaving from lane to lane is dangerous; pick a lane moving at the pace you want and stay in it.

teaching.text: Lane hopping is dangerous on a freeway, so choose a lane that suits your pace and stay with it. Remember: pick a lane, stay.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Weaving from lane to lane is dangerous; pick a lane moving at the pace you want and stay in it.

question.text: What must you do before changing lanes to pass or exit?

answer.text: When you must change lanes to pass or exit, check traffic carefully and signal well before you move.

teaching.text: Before changing lanes to pass or exit, check traffic carefully and turn on your signal well ahead. Remember: check, then signal early.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When you must change lanes to pass or exit, check traffic carefully and signal well before you move.

question.text: What should you do if you break down on a freeway?

answer.text: In a freeway breakdown, park completely off the traveled lanes and stay with the vehicle if you possibly can.

teaching.text: If the car breaks down, get it completely off the traveled lanes and stay with it if you can. Remember: fully off, stay put.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a freeway breakdown, park completely off the traveled lanes and stay with the vehicle if you possibly can.

question.text: What distress signals tell officers you need help on a freeway?

answer.text: The distress signals are an open trunk, a raised hood if weather allows, and a white cloth tied to a door handle or antenna, and an officer who sees them will help.

teaching.text: Signal distress with an open trunk, a raised hood if weather allows, and a white cloth, and call the troopers at star H P. Remember: trunk, hood, white cloth.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The distress signals are an open trunk, a raised hood if weather allows, and a white cloth tied to a door handle or antenna, and an officer who sees them will help.

question.text: When may you park on a freeway?

answer.text: Parking on the freeway is not allowed except in an emergency.

teaching.text: The freeway is no place to park, except in a real emergency. Remember: emergencies only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking on the freeway is not allowed except in an emergency.

question.text: What are entrance ramps and acceleration lanes for?

answer.text: Entrance ramps are short one-way ramps that lead to an acceleration lane, where you speed up to match through traffic if possible.

teaching.text: Short one-way entrance ramps lead to an acceleration lane, where you bring your speed up to match traffic. Remember: speed up to match.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Entrance ramps are short one-way ramps that lead to an acceleration lane, where you speed up to match through traffic if possible.

question.text: How do you merge from the acceleration lane?

answer.text: From the acceleration lane, watch for a gap, signal, and merge smoothly into traffic.

teaching.text: In the acceleration lane, look for a gap, signal, and blend into traffic smoothly. Remember: gap, signal, merge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: From the acceleration lane, watch for a gap, signal, and merge smoothly into traffic.

question.text: Who yields when a driver enters the freeway?

answer.text: Freeway drivers should leave room for merging traffic, but an entering driver must yield if they do not.

teaching.text: Freeway drivers should leave room, but if they do not, the entering driver must yield. Remember: entering driver yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Freeway drivers should leave room for merging traffic, but an entering driver must yield if they do not.

question.text: Should you stop in the acceleration lane?

answer.text: Do not stop completely in the acceleration lane unless it is absolutely necessary.

teaching.text: Avoid stopping in the acceleration lane unless you absolutely must. Remember: keep rolling, do not stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not stop completely in the acceleration lane unless it is absolutely necessary.

question.text: What do you do at an entrance ramp with a YIELD sign and no acceleration lane?

answer.text: On an entrance ramp with a YIELD sign and no acceleration lane, entering drivers obey the sign and stop if needed instead of forcing their way in.

teaching.text: At a ramp with a YIELD sign and no acceleration lane, obey the sign and stop if needed instead of forcing your way in. Remember: yield sign, stop if needed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On an entrance ramp with a YIELD sign and no acceleration lane, entering drivers obey the sign and stop if needed instead of forcing their way in.

question.text: What is an interchange?

answer.text: An interchange joins two highways at different levels with separate connecting roads, so vehicles can cross, enter or leave without interfering with others.

teaching.text: An interchange connects highways at different levels with separate ramps so traffic can cross, enter and leave without conflict. Remember: highways crossing at levels.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An interchange joins two highways at different levels with separate connecting roads, so vehicles can cross, enter or leave without interfering with others.

question.text: What are the four common interchange types?

answer.text: Four common interchange types are directional, cloverleaf, diamond and trumpet.

teaching.text: The four common interchanges are the directional, the cloverleaf, the diamond and the trumpet. Remember: directional, clover, diamond, trumpet.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Four common interchange types are directional, cloverleaf, diamond and trumpet.

question.text: What does a directional interchange serve?

answer.text: A directional interchange serves heavy traffic moving between only two legs, with other movements handled by ordinary diamond-type ramps.

teaching.text: A directional interchange is built for heavy traffic moving between just two legs. Remember: heavy traffic, two legs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A directional interchange serves heavy traffic moving between only two legs, with other movements handled by ordinary diamond-type ramps.

question.text: What does a cloverleaf interchange use, and what does it remove?

answer.text: A cloverleaf interchange uses loop connections for turns on and off the freeway from four directions and removes left-turn and cross-traffic conflicts.

teaching.text: A cloverleaf uses loops for turns from four directions and removes left-turn and cross-traffic conflicts. Remember: loops remove left turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A cloverleaf interchange uses loop connections for turns on and off the freeway from four directions and removes left-turn and cross-traffic conflicts.

question.text: How does a diamond interchange work?

answer.text: A diamond interchange has four ramps for entering or leaving with the flow, and left turns are made after you leave the freeway.

teaching.text: A diamond interchange has four ramps, and left turns happen after you leave the freeway. Remember: four ramps, left after exit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A diamond interchange has four ramps for entering or leaving with the flow, and left turns are made after you leave the freeway.

question.text: When is a trumpet interchange used?

answer.text: A trumpet interchange gives freeway access where another road meets it in a T, as a variation of the directional or diamond design.

teaching.text: A trumpet interchange serves a road that meets the freeway in a T. Remember: T junction access.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A trumpet interchange gives freeway access where another road meets it in a T, as a variation of the directional or diamond design.

question.text: Where do left turns happen at a diamond interchange?

answer.text: A diamond interchange lets you enter and leave with the flow on four ramps, and any left turn comes only after you are off the freeway, never on it.

teaching.text: At a diamond interchange you leave the freeway first, then make any left turn on the crossing road. Remember: off the freeway first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A diamond interchange lets you enter and leave with the flow on four ramps, and any left turn comes only after you are off the freeway, never on it.

question.text: How should you prepare for a freeway exit?

answer.text: Plan your exit early and watch the signs, moving into the proper lane well ahead of time.

teaching.text: Plan your exit early, follow the signs and get into the proper lane well before you reach it. Remember: plan early, move early.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Plan your exit early and watch the signs, moving into the proper lane well ahead of time.

question.text: Where should you slow down when exiting a freeway?

answer.text: To exit, signal, enter the deceleration lane and slow there, never slowing suddenly on the freeway itself, and be ready to yield or stop at the end of the ramp.

teaching.text: Signal and slow down in the deceleration lane, not on the freeway, and be ready to yield or stop at the ramp's end. Remember: slow in the exit lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To exit, signal, enter the deceleration lane and slow there, never slowing suddenly on the freeway itself, and be ready to yield or stop at the end of the ramp.

question.text: What should you do if you miss your exit?

answer.text: If you miss your exit, do not stop, back up or turn around; go on to the next exit and come back.

teaching.text: Missed your exit? Do not stop, back up or turn around; continue to the next exit and come back. Remember: next exit, come back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you miss your exit, do not stop, back up or turn around; go on to the next exit and come back.

question.text: What must a vehicle have to be driven safely?

answer.text: You cannot be a safe driver unless your vehicle is properly equipped and mechanically sound, and Alabama law sets the safety equipment required.

teaching.text: A safe driver needs a vehicle that is properly equipped and mechanically sound, as Alabama law requires. Remember: sound car, legal gear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You cannot be a safe driver unless your vehicle is properly equipped and mechanically sound, and Alabama law sets the safety equipment required.

question.text: What two brakes must every automobile have?

answer.text: Every automobile needs two separate ways of applying the brakes: a regular foot brake and a parking brake.

teaching.text: Every automobile needs both a foot brake and a parking brake. Remember: foot brake plus parking brake.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every automobile needs two separate ways of applying the brakes: a regular foot brake and a parking brake.

question.text: What must a muffler do, and which devices are forbidden?

answer.text: Every vehicle needs a working muffler that stops excessive or unusual noise, and muffler cutouts, bypasses and similar devices are forbidden.

teaching.text: A working muffler must keep noise down, and cutouts or bypasses are forbidden. Remember: quiet muffler, no cutouts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every vehicle needs a working muffler that stops excessive or unusual noise, and muffler cutouts, bypasses and similar devices are forbidden.

question.text: What must the exhaust system not do?

answer.text: The exhaust system must not leak carbon monoxide into the vehicle and should be checked periodically.

teaching.text: The exhaust must not leak carbon monoxide into the car, so have it checked periodically. Remember: no fumes inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The exhaust system must not leak carbon monoxide into the vehicle and should be checked periodically.

question.text: What must a vehicle with a windshield have?

answer.text: Any motor vehicle with a windshield must have wipers in good working order.

teaching.text: If a vehicle has a windshield, it must have wipers in good working order. Remember: working wipers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Any motor vehicle with a windshield must have wipers in good working order.

question.text: How far behind must your rear view mirrors let you see?

answer.text: All vehicles must have rear view mirrors that let the driver see two hundred feet behind.

teaching.text: Rear view mirrors must let the driver see two hundred feet behind. Remember: mirror sees two hundred.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: All vehicles must have rear view mirrors that let the driver see two hundred feet behind.

question.text: Which lights must a motor vehicle have?

answer.text: Required lighting includes a minimum of two white headlights, one or more red taillights, a brake light, and a light over the rear license plate.

teaching.text: The car must have at least two white headlights, red taillights, a brake light and a rear plate light. Remember: two head, tail, brake, plate.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Required lighting includes a minimum of two white headlights, one or more red taillights, a brake light, and a light over the rear license plate.

question.text: How far must lights be visible, and how far must high beams reach?

answer.text: All lights must be visible from at least five hundred feet, and the high beam must light objects at least three hundred fifty feet away and stay properly aimed.

teaching.text: All lights must be visible from five hundred feet, and high beams must reach three hundred fifty feet and stay aimed. Remember: five hundred seen, three fifty lit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: All lights must be visible from at least five hundred feet, and the high beam must light objects at least three hundred fifty feet away and stay properly aimed.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: five hundred seen, three fifty lit

question.text: May you flash both turn signals to warn of a hazard?

answer.text: Flashing both turn signals, or another pair of lights, at the same time to warn of a vehicle hazard is permitted.

teaching.text: Flashing both turn signals together to warn of a vehicle hazard is allowed. Remember: hazard flashers allowed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Flashing both turn signals, or another pair of lights, at the same time to warn of a vehicle hazard is permitted.

question.text: How do the mirror, light visibility and high beam distances compare?

answer.text: Rear view mirrors must show two hundred feet behind, while every light must be visible from five hundred feet and high beams must reach three hundred fifty feet.

teaching.text: Two hundred feet is for mirrors, five hundred for light visibility, and three hundred fifty for high beam reach. Remember: two hundred, five hundred, three fifty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Rear view mirrors must show two hundred feet behind, while every light must be visible from five hundred feet and high beams must reach three hundred fifty feet.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: two hundred, five hundred, three fifty

question.text: How do safety belts help in crashes?

answer.text: In crashes, steering assemblies cause thirty percent of fatal injuries and hitting the windshield, its frame or the dash causes another forty percent, second collisions that safety belts can prevent.

teaching.text: Belts prevent the second collisions with the steering assembly, windshield, frame or dash that cause most crash deaths. Remember: belts stop second collisions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In crashes, steering assemblies cause thirty percent of fatal injuries and hitting the windshield, its frame or the dash causes another forty percent, second collisions that safety belts can prevent.

question.text: What do children under six need in a car?

answer.text: Children under six years old need special child and infant restraints to protect them from serious injury or death.

teaching.text: Children under six need special child and infant restraints to stay safe in a crash. Remember: special seats under six.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Children under six years old need special child and infant restraints to protect them from serious injury or death.

question.text: Why do small children need restraints?

answer.text: Traffic crashes are the leading killer of children, and child and infant restraints keep small children from becoming flying missiles in a crash.

teaching.text: Crashes are the leading killer of children, and proper restraints keep them from being thrown like missiles. Remember: no flying missiles.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traffic crashes are the leading killer of children, and child and infant restraints keep small children from becoming flying missiles in a crash.

question.text: Which vehicles may use bells, sirens or exhaust whistles?

answer.text: Every motor vehicle needs a working horn, and bells, sirens or exhaust whistles are allowed only on emergency vehicles.

teaching.text: Every vehicle needs a working horn, while sirens, bells and exhaust whistles belong only on emergency vehicles. Remember: sirens for emergencies only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every motor vehicle needs a working horn, and bells, sirens or exhaust whistles are allowed only on emergency vehicles.

question.text: When may you use your horn?

answer.text: Use the horn only to give a warning reasonably needed for safety, never to announce arrival or call passengers, because needless use can lead to arrest.

teaching.text: Honk only to give a warning needed for safety, never to announce yourself or call passengers. Remember: horn for warnings only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use the horn only to give a warning reasonably needed for safety, never to announce arrival or call passengers, because needless use can lead to arrest.

question.text: How should you care for your tires?

answer.text: Buy tires rated to carry your car's weight, check pressure often, never drive on under-inflated tires, and have uneven wear checked for wheel or alignment problems.

teaching.text: Use tires rated for your car's weight, check pressure often, never run them under-inflated, and check uneven wear. Remember: right tires, right pressure.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Buy tires rated to carry your car's weight, check pressure often, never drive on under-inflated tires, and have uneven wear checked for wheel or alignment problems.

question.text: When is a tire illegal?

answer.text: A tire is illegal once its tread is less than one or sixteen inch deep.

teaching.text: Once the tread is worn below the legal minimum depth, the tire is illegal to use. Remember: too little tread, illegal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A tire is illegal once its tread is less than one or sixteen inch deep.

question.text: How can you treat your tires kindly?

answer.text: Avoid jack-rabbit starts and screeching stops unless truly necessary, go easy on corners and rough roads, let tires cool on long hot trips, and check the spare now and then.

teaching.text: Skip jack-rabbit starts and screeching stops, take corners and rough roads gently, and let tires cool on hot trips. Remember: no jack-rabbit starts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Avoid jack-rabbit starts and screeching stops unless truly necessary, go easy on corners and rough roads, let tires cool on long hot trips, and check the spare now and then.

question.text: May you use different types of tires?

answer.text: Never use different types of tires, and ask your dealer before mixing types between front and back.

teaching.text: Do not mix different tire types, and talk to your dealer before mixing front and back. Remember: never mix tire types.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never use different types of tires, and ask your dealer before mixing types between front and back.

question.text: Why does maintenance matter?

answer.text: Brakes, exhaust, cooling systems, lights, wipers and tires wear out, and any one left unmaintained could cause a serious crash, so have the car checked.

teaching.text: Brakes, exhaust, cooling, lights, wipers and tires wear out, and any neglected one can cause a serious crash. Remember: worn parts cause crashes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Brakes, exhaust, cooling systems, lights, wipers and tires wear out, and any one left unmaintained could cause a serious crash, so have the car checked.

question.text: How should you plan a freeway trip?

answer.text: Plan freeway trips with a map, deciding exactly where you will get on and off.

teaching.text: Before a freeway trip, use a map to decide exactly where you will get on and off. Remember: map your on and off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Plan freeway trips with a map, deciding exactly where you will get on and off.

question.text: What should you check before a freeway trip?

answer.text: Check fuel, water and oil before a freeway trip, because no service stations sit directly on freeways, and check every tire, including the spare.

teaching.text: Fill up and check water, oil and every tire, including the spare, because service stations are not on the freeway. Remember: fuel, water, oil, tires.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Check fuel, water and oil before a freeway trip, because no service stations sit directly on freeways, and check every tire, including the spare.

question.text: Where are most children hurt in pupil transportation?

answer.text: Most children hurt or killed in pupil transportation are outside the bus, struck by drivers who ignore its flashing red lights and stop arm, in the area called the DEATH ZONE.

teaching.text: Most children hurt in pupil transportation are struck outside the bus by drivers ignoring its red lights and stop arm. Remember: outside the bus, death zone.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Most children hurt or killed in pupil transportation are outside the bus, struck by drivers who ignore its flashing red lights and stop arm, in the area called the DEATH ZONE.

recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of leaving the freeway. Plan exits early, slow only in the deceleration lane, and go on to the next exit if you miss yours. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of required vehicle equipment. Cars need two brakes, a quiet muffler, working wipers, mirrors that see two hundred feet, and lights visible from five hundred feet. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of belts, horns and tires. Belts prevent second collisions, small children need special restraints, horns are only for warnings, and tires need enough tread. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.
